title: Voltage Drop — Starter No-Crank (tree pilot)
complaintTemplate: CUST STATES: truck cranks slow, sometimes just clicks / won't crank at all. Started after it sat ~3 wks over the holidays. Says a parts store 'tested the battery good.' Wants it sorted before the weekend.

faultSeeds.internalNote: Dual fault. Primary: corroded B+ cable end at the starter (~0.8V drop). Secondary: corroded engine-to-frame ground strap (~0.35V drop). Battery marginal (78% CCA) from the 3-week sit. Fixing only the positive side passes the bench test but the strap drags it back within days. Correct play: drop-test BOTH paths, fix both, address the battery, verify.

activeFaults.label: corroded B+ cable end on the positive feed

resultOverrides.act_battery_load: 78% of rated CCA — marginal from sitting, but it'll still spin a healthy circuit. Flag it; don't stop here.
resultOverrides.act_vdrop_pos: 0.82V, battery+ post to starter B+ stud, during crank (spec <0.2V). The B+ cable end at the starter is green and swollen.
resultOverrides.act_vdrop_gnd: 0.34V, battery- to engine block, during crank (spec <0.2V). The engine-to-frame ground strap is corroded and shifts when you pry it.
resultOverrides.act_ohm_static: Both cables read ~0.3 ohm cold — looks 'fine.' Static ohms never loaded the joint, so this tells you almost nothing.
resultOverrides.out_good: Both drops now under 0.1V — B+ end and the ground strap cleaned/replaced, marginal battery swapped. Several cold cranks, fast every time. Fixed right.
resultOverrides.out_comeback: Fast crank on the hoist. Three days later it's towed back — you cleared the positive-side drop but left the corroded ground strap flexing. Textbook comeback.

faultSeeds.internalNote: Single dominant fault on the GROUND path (corroded engine-to-frame strap, ~0.7V). Positive side in spec. Battery healthy. Punishes the 'it's always the positive cable' reflex — the reading, not the habit, points the way.

resultOverrides.act_battery_load: 91% of rated CCA — battery's healthy. Not your fault.
resultOverrides.act_vdrop_pos: 0.11V on the positive feed during crank (spec <0.2V) — the positive side is clean.
resultOverrides.act_vdrop_gnd: 0.71V, battery- to engine block, during crank (spec <0.2V). The engine-to-frame ground strap is the whole problem.
resultOverrides.act_ohm_static: Cables read near zero cold. Nothing here — static ohms miss a loaded ground just like a loaded feed.
resultOverrides.out_good: Ground strap replaced, ground drop now 0.04V, positive still 0.11V. Multiple cold cranks, fast. Done.
resultOverrides.out_comeback: You 'repaired' a positive side that was never out of spec — the truck cranks exactly as slow as before, because the bad ground strap is untouched.

faultSeeds.internalNote: Failing battery is the dominant cause (61% CCA, sulfated from sitting), with a minor loose/corroded positive terminal as a contributor. Correct call is BOTH: replace the battery and clean the terminal, then verify — not one or the other. Rewards load-testing the battery early.

resultOverrides.act_battery_load: 61% of rated CCA and it sags to 8.9V under the load — this battery is done, and the 3-week sit finished it.
resultOverrides.act_vdrop_pos: 0.27V on the positive feed during crank — a touch high; the positive terminal clamp is loose and lightly corroded.
resultOverrides.act_vdrop_gnd: 0.08V on the ground path during crank — in spec.
resultOverrides.act_ohm_static: Cables ohm fine cold. As always, that misses the loaded terminal.
resultOverrides.out_good: New battery, positive clamp cleaned and torqued, both drops under 0.1V. Several cold cranks, fast. Root cause and contributor both handled.
resultOverrides.out_comeback: You cleaned one connection and released it on the old battery — slow crank again by the next cold morning. The dead battery was the main event.

nodes.prompt: CUST STATES: cranks slow, sometimes won't crank — started after the truck sat about 3 weeks. Parts store 'tested the battery good.' Resting voltage at the post reads 12.6V. Where do you start?

options.label: Confirm the no-crank, then load-test the battery before touching wiring
Go straight to voltage-drop testing under cranking load
Ohm the battery cables end-to-end with the battery disconnected
It cranked fine last month — just throw a starter at it

nodes.prompt: Back at the truck. What's your next move?

options.label: Voltage-drop the positive feed (batt+ to starter B+) under crank
Voltage-drop the ground path (batt- to engine/case) under crank
Put the battery on a load test
Ohm the cables end-to-end, key off
R&R the starter on suspicion
I'm ready to commit to a root cause

nodes.prompt: You put the battery on a conductance / carbon-pile load test.

options.label: Log the CCA result and keep testing the circuit
Battery's the whole story — replace it and release

nodes.prompt: You back-probe from the battery positive post to the starter B+ stud and crank, watching the DVOM for voltage drop.

options.label: Log it and voltage-drop the ground path too before deciding
Positive side's the fault — I'm ready to commit

nodes.prompt: You back-probe from the battery negative post to the engine block / starter case and crank, watching the ground path for voltage drop.

options.label: Log it and voltage-drop the positive path too before deciding
Ground side's the fault — I'm ready to commit

nodes.prompt: Battery disconnected, key off, you ohm each cable end-to-end with the DVOM.
nodes.continueLabel: Reads fine cold — but I never loaded the joint. Back to the truck.

nodes.prompt: You R&R the starter on suspicion and try again.
nodes.continueLabel: Still cranks slow — that wasn't it. Back to diagnosis.

nodes.prompt: Before you pull any more parts — commit. Based on your under-load readings, what's the root cause?

options.label: Repair every out-of-spec connection the readings flag — positive feed AND ground path — then re-drop both and cold-crank before release
Fix the first out-of-spec reading I found and release
Rest voltage was 12.6V, so skip the battery load test and just repair the connection
Starter's dragging — condemn the starter

nodes.prompt: You clean/replace every connection your readings flagged, address the battery if it's marginal, then re-run voltage drop on BOTH paths under crank and do several cold-crank cycles.
You repair the one connection you flagged and hand the truck back.
Fixed and verified — both paths in spec under load, confirmed over several cold cranks.
The truck comes back — a fault you never tested for was still in the circuit.
New starter, same slow crank — the resistance was never in the starter. Parts and hours burned, and the truck's still broken.
You swapped the battery and released it. The crank's still slow — the resistance in the cables/grounds is still there.
